body.text: Stablecoin market cap has slid to a six-month low near $287B (down ~$16B in 10 weeks) as the GENIUS Act's ban on payment-stablecoin yields pushes capital toward tokenized Treasuries.
Tether Launches USAT, Enters US Market Head-On With Circle
Tether's new USAT stablecoin, issued via Anchorage Digital Bank under the GENIUS Act framework, marks its first regulated US product and a direct challenge to Circle's USDC dominance.
Treasury Proposes GENIUS Act Rules After Missing Deadline
US Treasury issued proposed stablecoin issuer rules on Aug 17 after six federal agencies failed to finalize a coordinated package by the July 18 statutory deadline; comment period runs into August.
Stablecoin Market Cap Slides to Six-Month Low
Total stablecoin market cap fell to roughly $287B, down $16B over 10 weeks, as GENIUS Act's yield ban on payment stablecoins pushes capital into tokenized Treasuries.

Attackers exploiting a five-year-old firmware flaw in Coinkite's Coldcard wallets have drained over $130M (1,800+ BTC) from 5,200+ addresses across four waves since July 30; Coinkite has pushed emergency patches.
macOS Screen-Sharing Flaw Exploited for Covert Monero Mining
Hackers abused CVE-2026-65400, a now-patched macOS screen-sharing vulnerability, to remotely hijack Macs with exposed port 5900 and mine Monero without owners' knowledge.
Crypto project hacks totaled $1.32B in the first half of 2026; April alone saw over $600M stolen across ~30 incidents, including the $285M Drift and $293M Kelp DAO exploits.
